chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: How Herman and Ralph Burns worked: Herman as editor
summary: Herman suggested only tempo for a tune; Burns brought the arrangement and invited him to remove anything that didn't work, giving Herman confidence as an editor.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yes. You mentioned some of these things during your 40th anniversary, that you were reflecting back because he was coming back for the guest shot and so forth. Some of the ways you worked together -- how did you -- did you just leave it to his control? How much control and leadership did you exercise as far as direction?
Well, we had a very strange arrangement. I don't think anyone else in the music business probably had it quite like this, because I never heard about it.

In the first place, I -- my only commitment as far as what we were to do, starting with the basic material, if I came in with a tune that I felt had some possibilities, I might suggest that it might be nice done slowly, or it might be nice done at a swinging tempo, and that was it. And I'll see you later.
And then, when he would bring in that arrangement,

or any other arrangement, he would say, "Woody, this sort of goes like this or like this, " and then he might play me a little bit of it. And then he said, "And anything you don't think makes it, take it out."

And he is the one that gave me the confidence to imagine that I was an editor, because he was his very personal attitude of -- and later he would say, "That was fine, I'm glad you took that out, " or something, words to that effect, which gave me great confidence. Maybe it was undeserved, but at least I felt I wasn't -- we certainly weren't battling each other.

And sometimes I would like some phrase or some little thing and I would ask him to repeat it several times. And he probably thought I was mad with that, too, but I also thought that maybe it gave the thing a certain charm or something. No, I think we were -- I've always felt that we never had to worry about each other's weaknesses or strengths, you know, like, we could say just anything that came into our heads and it would be fine.
We don't have many of those associations in life.
